overview.intro: Confirmed attacks affected hospital care, online stores, surveillance cameras and personal data. Investigations are still determining the full scope of several incidents.

items.headline: New Mexico hospital diverts ambulances after cybersecurity incident
items.what_happened: The University of New Mexico Health System experienced a cybersecurity incident on Monday, October 26. Its main hospital stopped accepting some patients, more than 30 clinics canceled appointments, and classes were canceled. The FBI is assisting an active investigation.
items.impact: Ambulances were sent elsewhere, temporarily leaving New Mexico without an emergency department able to handle the most serious injuries. Hospitals and clinics began reopening in stages later Monday. The health system’s Level 1 trauma center was affected.
items.what_next: Watch for service-restoration notices and investigation updates from UNM. The cause, scope and any theft of patient, employee or student information remain under investigation.

items.headline: Hackers confirmed running commands through widely used website software
items.what_happened: Researchers confirmed successful attacks against decoy systems using two flaws in widely used PHP website software. The activity was recorded on October 24, after scanning and unsuccessful attempts had already been seen. The affected software versions were fixed October 21.
items.impact: This does not show that ordinary websites were compromised, but it raises the risk for websites still running affected versions. PHP supports a large share of websites, including services people use for shopping and information.
items.what_next: U.S. government agencies have until October 29 to apply fixes. Researchers are watching for attacks against real websites and for evidence that attackers downloaded additional malware.

items.headline: Nearly 1,000 online stores carry hidden code aimed at shoppers
items.what_happened: A campaign active since July 2025 infected 953 online stores, mostly using Magento. The stores were altered to load attacker-controlled code only for real visitors, helping it avoid security checks. The final harmful payload has not been identified.
items.impact: Shoppers may face redirects, scams or attempts to steal information, although the reporting does not confirm what the code ultimately did. Store owners may need to take sites offline while investigating, potentially delaying orders.
items.what_next: Researchers are checking whether the campaign is still spreading and what the hidden code delivers. Customers should be cautious if a store behaves unusually or asks for unexpected payment or account details.

items.headline: Ukraine warns that hackers are taking over connected security cameras
items.what_happened: Ukraine’s CERT-UA confirmed cases involving Dahua cameras and recorders. Attackers accessed video, changed settings and created accounts. The incidents were reported last week; the number of affected devices, targets and responsible group remain unknown.
items.impact: Compromised cameras could expose homes, businesses, government sites or military-related activity. The warning does not confirm that any particular public facility or military camera was affected.
items.what_next: Ukrainian authorities are investigating whether the activity connects to an earlier campaign that compromised more than 14,500 cameras between June and July. Camera owners may see service or viewing changes while systems are secured.

items.headline: University of Copenhagen says data on 525,000 people was accessed
items.what_happened: Hackers entered a university test environment containing personal information. The university detected the breach on October 20 and disclosed it on October 23. A later update added 20,000 staff and students whose building-access PINs may have been exposed.
items.impact: Names, national identity numbers, contact details and some access codes may be at risk. The university says daily operations were not disrupted and there is no indication that operational systems were accessed.
items.what_next: The university is still determining the full scope and is replacing access codes while reopening restricted areas. Affected people should be wary of convincing messages asking for information or access.

finance.intro: No confirmed banking or payment-system outage was reported. Online-store compromises create a possible shopping and payment risk, but theft was not confirmed.

items.headline: Compromised online stores may expose shoppers to scams
items.what_happened: Attackers planted hidden browser code on 953 online stores. It was designed to distinguish real shoppers from security scanners, but researchers have not captured the final payload.
items.impact: Customers could encounter redirects or attempts to collect payment or account details. The reports do not confirm stolen card data or payment failures.
items.what_next: Investigators are working to identify the final payload and remaining affected stores. Shoppers should verify unusual payment prompts through the store’s normal website or app.

healthcare.intro: A cybersecurity incident disrupted the largest hospital system in New Mexico. Separate healthcare data exposures affected plan members and patients, without reported care outages.

items.headline: New Mexico hospital resumes services in stages after cyber incident
items.what_happened: UNM Health System diverted ambulances, canceled appointments at more than 30 clinics and canceled classes on October 26. Hospitals and clinics later began reopening in phases.
items.impact: Emergency care and routine appointments were disrupted. Other New Mexico hospital systems accepted additional patients. The incident’s cause and data impact remain unclear.
items.what_next: Watch for service-restoration notices and investigation updates from UNM. The cause, scope and any theft of patient, employee or student information remain under investigation.

items.headline: Vendor access incident affects 238,083 Denver health-plan members
items.what_happened: A vendor’s access key was publicly exposed for more than a year and could have opened a read-only database containing Denver Health Medical Plan information. The plan has not found evidence that the key was misused.
items.impact: Names, dates of birth, eligibility, provider and health measurements may have been exposed. Financial details and Social Security numbers were not involved, and data could not be changed or deleted through the key.
items.what_next: Denver Health Medical Plan is notifying affected people while the investigation continues. Recipients should watch for targeted health-related scams or messages requesting account information.

internet.intro: Confirmed incidents included a hospital disruption, compromised websites, hacked cameras and exposed university data. No broad communications outage was reported.

items.headline: Hackers took over Dahua cameras in Ukraine
items.what_happened: CERT-UA reported unauthorized access to Dahua cameras and recorders, including viewing video, changing settings and adding accounts. The timing and number of affected devices are unknown.
items.impact: Private, business or government surveillance footage could be exposed. The report does not confirm effects on public internet or camera services.
items.what_next: Authorities are investigating the scope and whether it matches an earlier campaign affecting more than 14,500 devices. Further findings may clarify which owners are affected.

items.headline: University test system breach puts personal data at risk
items.what_happened: The University of Copenhagen confirmed unauthorized access to a test environment holding data on 525,000 people, later adding 20,000 people whose access PINs may have been exposed.
items.impact: Names, national identity numbers, contact details and some building-access information may be used for phishing or impersonation. University operations were not disrupted.
items.what_next: The university is replacing access codes and continuing its investigation. Affected students and staff should verify unexpected messages independently.

supply_chain.intro: A vendor-related healthcare data incident affected Denver Health members. This was an exposed supplier key, not a compromise of widely distributed software.

items.headline: Exposed vendor key may have opened Denver health-plan data
items.what_happened: SquareML, a healthcare analytics supplier, accidentally placed an access key on a public website in June 2025. Denver Health Medical Plan learned of the exposure on August 14, 2026, and disabled the key on August 18.
items.impact: The key could provide read-only access to information on 238,083 members. The plan found no evidence of misuse, and records could not be changed, deleted or exported through the key.
items.what_next: Denver Health is notifying affected members while the investigation continues. People receiving notices should be alert for health-insurance impersonation attempts.

overview.intro: New reports describe data exposure at a developer platform, repeated breaches involving UK police suppliers, customer information stolen from an energy company, and a hardware-wallet verification compromise. An international operation also cut criminals off from 180,000 infected computers. Several incidents caused no reported service outage.

items.headline: Warp says a vendor breach exposed some AI activity records
items.what_happened: Warp said an attack on a third-party vendor exposed agent decision logs and usage data for about 1% of its users. The incident was detected Friday, and outside investigators and law enforcement are involved.
items.impact: Warp has not said whether source code, prompts, passwords or other sensitive data were exposed. The company says it contained the incident and notified users it identified as affected. The platform has at least 800,000 users.
items.what_next: The investigation should clarify the affected users and the types of data exposed. Warp may provide further notices if more sensitive information is found.

items.headline: UK watchdog finds repeated breaches of suppliers holding police data
items.what_happened: A UK policing watchdog reported multiple cyberattacks since 2021 against suppliers that held police information. It did not identify the suppliers, count the attacks or confirm whether data was stolen.
items.impact: The report says some attacks affected operational systems, data or services, but the public impact of the supplier breaches is unclear. Police recorded 252 cybersecurity incidents in the first three months of 2026, plus 796 near misses.
items.what_next: The investigation and oversight work may clarify which police forces, suppliers and records were affected. The watchdog warned that further attacks are highly likely.

items.headline: Energy customers in France have data stolen through a partner platform
items.what_happened: Attackers accessed a marketing platform used by ENGIE’s business partners and stole customer information. ENGIE said the company’s internal systems were not breached and the incident is limited to customers in France.
items.impact: Names, addresses, contact details and energy contract information were exposed. No banking data was involved, and there is no report of power or gas service disruption.
items.what_next: ENGIE has contacted affected customers and notified authorities. Further details, including the number of people affected, may emerge from the investigation.

items.headline: Hardware-wallet maker replaces verification key after website breach
items.what_happened: Keystone said attackers obtained the key used to verify that its cryptocurrency hardware wallets are genuine, through a weakness in a third-party monitoring tool. Customer shipping records were also accessed.
items.impact: A counterfeit wallet using the old key could pass the online check and potentially steal cryptocurrency, but Keystone reported no counterfeit devices or thefts. The breach exposed records for 25,964 buyers and 12,873 abandoned checkouts; payment and bank details were not involved.
items.what_next: Keystone is destroying 18,835 unsold devices, replacing the verification key and contacting affected customers. Orders are paused while devices using the new key are prepared.

items.headline: Australia cuts malware criminals off from 180,000 infected computers
items.what_happened: Australia’s Signals Directorate gained access to a criminal control system for the Amadey malware and disconnected it from about 180,000 infected computers worldwide. The malware had been used to install more malware and steal account details.
items.impact: The criminals can no longer use that particular system to issue commands or steal new information from those computers. Earlier theft may still be misused, and the operation did not clean the infected devices.
items.what_next: Authorities may identify victims or related criminal infrastructure. People and organizations affected by the malware may continue receiving notifications as investigations develop.

overview.intro: New reports show a Japanese hosting provider confirming customer data exposure, a payment-data theft campaign through a shared shopping platform, and full recovery after Monday’s New Mexico hospital disruption.

items.headline: Japanese hosting provider confirms customer data was published online
items.what_happened: GMO Internet said attackers who entered its Onamae Desktop Cloud stole and published company and customer data. The intrusion was detected October 20. The provider had warned that malware might have been placed on up to 26,739 customer servers.
items.impact: Customer payment information was not exposed, but trading-account details and MetaTrader sign-in information may have been. GMO says ransomware was not activated on customer machines, although service availability was reduced while servers were shut down.
items.what_next: GMO is scanning customer systems, checking the leaked data and working with Trend Micro. It may offer further compensation and replace computers damaged by any later ransomware activity.

items.headline: Shared shopping-platform code stole card details from Brazilian shoppers
items.what_happened: Attackers altered an analytics script used by Convertr, a Brazilian online-shopping platform serving dozens of major brands. The script loaded on merchants’ checkout pages and collected card numbers, expiration dates, security codes, names and taxpayer numbers. The campaign was found October 24.
items.impact: Some shoppers who paid by card through affected Brazilian stores may have had payment details captured. This is a confirmed payment-data theft campaign, but the number of affected shoppers and any resulting fraud are unclear.
items.what_next: Convertr removed the harmful code and upgraded the affected software. It is notifying merchants and payment providers. Investigators may clarify which stores and transactions were exposed.

items.headline: New Mexico hospital says patient care has fully returned to normal
items.what_happened: After Monday’s cyberattack, UNM Health said all critical electronic systems were back online Tuesday. Hospitals reopened fully, ambulance traffic returned to normal, and clinics resumed scheduled appointments and procedures.
items.impact: The earlier ambulance diversion, canceled appointments and suspended surgeries have ended. UNM said the event affected some end-user devices but did not reach core systems or servers. Claims by a ransomware group about stolen data remain unconfirmed.
items.what_next: UNM and law enforcement are still investigating the cause and scope. Patients, staff and students may receive further notices if investigators confirm information exposure.

finance.intro: Confirmed payment-data theft affected a shared Brazilian shopping platform. A separate Japanese hosting incident may expose trading-account details, but no banking or payment data was reported stolen.

items.headline: Brazilian checkout script captured shoppers’ payment details
items.what_happened: A compromised analytics script used by Convertr-loaded online stores collected card information during checkout. Convertr removed the script after the campaign was identified October 24.
items.impact: Card payments made through some affected Brazilian stores may be exposed. Confirmed financial losses and the number of affected shoppers are not known.
items.what_next: Merchants and payment providers are being notified. Further investigation may identify affected stores and transactions.

items.headline: Japanese cloud-service customers warned about exposed trading credentials
items.what_happened: GMO Internet said attackers stole and published company and customer data after entering its Onamae Desktop Cloud service. Trading-account details and MetaTrader sign-in information may be included.
items.impact: No payment information was exposed, according to GMO. The company has not confirmed misuse of trading accounts, but customer servers experienced reduced availability during the response.
items.what_next: GMO is verifying the leaked information and scanning customer systems. More details about affected accounts and compensation may follow.

healthcare.intro: UNM Health reports that the service disruption from Monday’s cyberattack has ended. The investigation and any data-exposure assessment continue.

items.headline: New Mexico hospital restores ambulances, clinics and surgeries
items.what_happened: UNM Health said hospitals are fully open, ambulance traffic is normal and clinics have resumed scheduled care after Monday’s attack.
items.impact: The earlier diversion of ambulances and cancellation of appointments and outpatient surgeries have stopped. UNM says core systems and servers were not penetrated, but some end-user devices were affected.
items.what_next: Law enforcement and UNM are continuing to determine what happened and whether information was taken. Additional notices may be issued if the scope changes.

internet.intro: A Japanese hosting provider confirmed a customer-data leak and continuing recovery work. A separate shared checkout service was used to steal payment information from online shoppers.

items.headline: Japanese hosting provider confirms data leak after customer-server incident
items.what_happened: GMO Internet said data belonging to the company and its Onamae Desktop Cloud customers was published online after an October 20 intrusion. Up to 26,739 customer servers may have received malware, according to the company’s earlier warning.
items.impact: Service availability was reduced while servers were shut down and examined. GMO says payment information was not exposed, but trading credentials and account details may have been.
items.what_next: The company is scanning systems, checking the authenticity of leaked data and working with outside investigators. It says ransomware has not been activated on customer machines.

items.headline: Compromised checkout script affected stores using a shared platform
items.what_happened: Attackers changed Convertr’s analytics script so it collected information entered by shoppers on checkout pages. The code was removed after the campaign was identified October 24.
items.impact: Some online shoppers in Brazil may have had card and identity details stolen. The number of affected stores and customers is not yet known.
items.what_next: Convertr is notifying merchants and payment providers while investigators determine the campaign’s reach.

supply_chain.intro: Two incidents involved upstream services used by other organizations: a Japanese hosting provider and a shared Brazilian shopping platform. Both created risks beyond a single company’s own systems.

items.headline: GMO cloud service breach put customer servers and data at risk
items.what_happened: Attackers breached Onamae Desktop Cloud, a Japanese virtual-server provider, and may have placed malware on customer servers. GMO later confirmed that company and customer data was published online.
items.impact: Customers faced reduced service availability while servers were shut down. Trading credentials may have been exposed, but payment information was not, according to GMO.
items.what_next: GMO is examining customer systems and leaked information. The extent of customer impact and any further compensation remain under review.

items.headline: Convertr platform breach exposed shoppers across multiple stores
items.what_happened: A malicious change to Convertr’s shared analytics script reached checkout pages for merchants using the platform. The script stole payment and identity details entered by shoppers.
items.impact: This was a confirmed compromise of a shared service, not just one online store. Affected merchants and the number of exposed shoppers are still unclear.
items.what_next: Convertr removed the code and upgraded the affected software. Merchant and payment-provider investigations may establish the full scope.

overview.intro: New reports describe a large government-data breach in Moldova, customer-record exposure at a Sony internet provider, stolen patient information through a healthcare vendor, and confirmed attacks on network firewalls. A Japanese hosting breach has also been linked to unauthorized trading on some customer accounts.

items.headline: Moldova restores public services after government data breach
items.what_happened: Attackers extracted information linked to about 750,000 identification numbers from Moldovan government services between October 19 and 23. Authorities say roughly 11 million requests were made and are investigating possible foreign involvement, without naming a country or group.
items.impact: The stolen information may include identity, health, benefits, pension, vehicle and financial records. Dozens of public services were disrupted, including permits and food-safety registrations. Most have since been secured and are being restored. Bank card data was not exposed, officials said.
items.what_next: Authorities are checking the remaining systems and investigating further attempts made after October 23. People may face convincing messages pretending to come from banks or government offices.

items.headline: Sony internet customers’ personal records exposed in breach
items.what_happened: Sony Network Communications confirmed that a breach exposed about 2.5 million records containing information on current and former customers. The supplied report does not yet describe the exact data fields or the incident date.
items.impact: Customer privacy is affected, but the available reporting does not confirm payment theft, service outages or misuse of the information.
items.what_next: Sony’s investigation should clarify which customers and records were involved and whether any further effects are found.

items.headline: Healthcare vendor breaches expose data on 341,000 children and families
items.what_happened: Two attackers exploited a flaw in Metabase, a third-party data-analysis tool used by Blueberry Pediatrics and prescription provider Photon. Blueberry learned of the first incident on August 22 and the second on August 24; the breach was reported publicly in this window.
items.impact: Names, birth dates, health-plan details, medical records, service charges and medication information were exposed. Financial information, Social Security numbers, photos and videos were not involved. Patient care disruption was not reported.
items.what_next: Blueberry has blocked access, fixed the vendor flaw and is reviewing the affected records. Some people may receive more than one breach notice.

items.headline: Japanese hosting breach linked to unauthorized trading on customer accounts
items.what_happened: Attackers breached GMO Internet’s Desktop Cloud hosting service and stole customer information. A broker said leaked trading logins were used to make unauthorized trades on some customers’ accounts. GMO shut down servers across its plans starting October 21.
items.impact: Trading customers may face account restrictions, losses or delays while brokers investigate. GMO says payment-card data was not stored there; the number of affected customers and qualifying trades remains unknown.
items.what_next: GMO and brokers are investigating the leaked data and trades. The company has not confirmed the full compensation scope or impact on other services.

items.headline: Attackers break into 25 firewalls, including a U.S.-linked network
items.what_happened: Researchers found attacks on 25 internet-facing firewalls in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea on October 23 and 24. Two systems belonged to a U.S. government-affiliated environment, where attackers reached an internal management server and searched for account credentials.
items.impact: The activity shows confirmed compromise of network equipment, but the reporting does not establish stolen data, broader access or disruption to public services. The suspected China-linked operation has not been definitively attributed.
items.what_next: The affected organization and investigators are assessing whether credentials or internal systems were successfully accessed. The full scope remains unclear.

overview.intro: New reporting confirms a customer-data breach at Japan Airlines, details a long-running espionage network targeting critical services, and reports a major international operation against cybercrime. Flight operations were not disrupted, but several incidents could lead to fraud or impersonation attempts.

items.headline: Japan Airlines says 92,000 customers’ reservation data was exposed
items.what_happened: Japan Airlines said hackers entered Amadeus, the outside provider running its reservation, ticketing and check-in systems. Data from 92,000 Japan Airlines and Japan Transocean Air customers was accessed. About 2,000 records also included passport numbers, frequent-flyer numbers, email addresses and phone numbers.
items.impact: Flights, ticketing and check-in were not disrupted. Credit-card numbers were not exposed. Affected customers face a higher risk of convincing phishing emails, calls or fake websites using travel details.
items.what_next: Japan Airlines says it will contact affected customers. The investigation should clarify how the provider was breached and whether additional customer records were accessed.

items.headline: Researchers uncover covert network used to reach critical services
items.what_happened: Researchers said the China-linked group known as Volt Typhoon used a rotating chain of hacked routers, connected devices and business systems to hide attacks. The network supported at least four attacks using previously unknown flaws against management systems and other high-value targets.
items.impact: Hundreds of organizations were identified across communications, government, defense, utilities, transportation, aviation, water and emergency services. The report does not describe a new public outage or confirm that any particular household service was disrupted.
items.what_next: Investigators may identify more victims and clarify what information or access was obtained. The findings point to continued concern for critical services during a future crisis, but do not confirm such disruption now.

items.headline: International operation reports 1,462 arrests in cybercrime crackdown
items.what_happened: Interpol’s third Operation Serengeti led to 1,462 arrests across 20 African countries and the United States. Authorities reported recovering $105 million in stolen funds.
items.impact: The operation may interrupt criminal groups involved in online fraud and related theft. The supplied report does not identify specific services, companies or customers affected by the arrests.
items.what_next: Authorities may announce further charges, victim notifications or recovered money as investigations continue.

internet.intro: Japan Airlines reported customer-data exposure through its reservation provider. Researchers also described a covert network used in attacks on communications and other critical infrastructure.

items.headline: Japan Airlines reports customer-data exposure through reservation provider
items.what_happened: Hackers accessed part of the reservation data held by Amadeus, affecting 92,000 Japan Airlines and Japan Transocean Air customers. About 2,000 records included more sensitive travel and contact details.
items.impact: Flight operations and credit-card systems were not affected. Customers may face targeted impersonation attempts using reservation or passport information.
items.what_next: Japan Airlines will contact affected customers while the provider and authorities investigate the breach.

items.headline: Covert hacking network reached high-value communications and utility targets
items.what_happened: Researchers said Volt Typhoon used compromised routers and other devices as temporary relays for attacks on telecommunications, government, defense, utilities, transportation, water and emergency services.
items.impact: The report identifies hundreds of victims but does not confirm a current public outage or a particular affected service. It shows that trusted network equipment can be used to conceal access to important organizations.
items.what_next: More victims and the extent of stolen information or retained access may be identified as investigations continue.

supply_chain.intro: A breach at the outside provider running Japan Airlines reservations exposed customer records. Researchers also described attacks that used compromised devices and management systems as stepping stones to high-value organizations.

items.headline: Japan Airlines customers affected through breached reservation provider
items.what_happened: Amadeus, an outside provider for reservations, ticketing and check-in, told Japan Airlines that hackers accessed customer reservation data for Japan Airlines and Japan Transocean Air flights.
items.impact: The airlines reported no flight disruption and no credit-card exposure. The incident affects customer privacy and may support targeted travel-related scams.
items.what_next: Japan Airlines and investigators are expected to clarify the provider breach and the full set of affected records.

items.headline: Researchers describe compromised devices used as attack relays
items.what_happened: Volt Typhoon reportedly routed attacks through hacked consumer, business and enterprise devices before targeting management platforms and high-value organizations. The compromised devices formed a temporary chain rather than a distributed software-update compromise.
items.impact: The activity affected organizations across communications, utilities, water, transportation, aviation and emergency services, but no new public-service outage was confirmed.
items.what_next: Investigations may establish which organizations retained unauthorized access and whether downstream data was taken.

overview.intro: Confirmed incidents this evening include a major cryptocurrency investigation, a short trading interruption, a Japanese internet-customer breach and a Belgian tax-service outage. Several events involve stolen personal or payment data, but the full effects remain under investigation.

items.headline: Binance investigates a possible cryptocurrency theft of billions
items.what_happened: Binance is investigating transfers from several of its digital-asset wallets. Blockchain researchers estimate that as much as $5.8 billion is linked to the suspected attacker, but Binance has not confirmed that the transfers were unauthorized or how much was stolen. Two stablecoin issuers froze more than $2.3 billion connected to the incident.
items.impact: Binance says customer funds are safe. The reported figure is not a confirmed loss, so the effect on customers is unclear. Frozen assets may limit further movement while the investigation continues.
items.what_next: Binance, law enforcement and blockchain analysts are checking whether the transfers were a breach and determining the actual amount involved. Customers should rely on official Binance notices, not unsolicited messages or links.

items.headline: Polymarket restores trading after a third-party script stole cryptocurrency
items.what_happened: A compromised website-monitoring provider supplied harmful code to Polymarket visitors. The code attempted to use logged-in trading sessions to sell positions and move cryptocurrency. Polymarket paused trading for about an hour on October 29, fixed the issue and said affected traders would be fully reimbursed.
items.impact: About $2.5 million in assets has been traced to a suspected attacker wallet, but Polymarket has not said how many users lost funds or the final amount. Trading is now back online. The incident involved a supplier used by the platform.
items.what_next: Polymarket and law enforcement are investigating the provider breach and reimbursement process. More users or affected amounts may be identified as the review continues.

items.headline: Sony’s Japanese internet provider confirms 2.6 million records were stolen
items.what_happened: Attackers entered the So-net member database on October 19. Sony Network Communications says records for about 2.14 million So-net customers and 443,000 Plala customers were taken. The data includes names, birth dates, contact details and internet connection IDs. Passwords for about 54,000 separate email accounts were also exposed.
items.impact: Affected email users were forced to change passwords because attackers could otherwise read or send messages. Sixteen records included bank-account details, but credit-card data and bank PINs were not stored. No internet outage was reported.
items.what_next: Sony is still investigating how the attackers got in and has reported the incident to Japan’s privacy regulator. Customers may receive further notices about exposed records or account protections.

items.headline: Belgium takes its main online tax portal offline after an attack
items.what_happened: Belgium’s finance ministry suspended MyMinfin on October 28 while investigating a cyberattack. The portal handles tax and other financial services. The shutdown came just before an October 31 filing deadline, and authorities said they would extend the deadline.
items.impact: People who use MyMinfin may be unable to file or manage tax matters online until services return. Officials said there is currently no indication that data was stolen. Other government applications remained fully or partly available.
items.what_next: Investigators are checking whether any information was exposed and when the portal can safely return. A revised filing deadline will be announced.

items.headline: Japan Airlines says its booking provider breach affected other airlines too
items.what_happened: A new report confirms that the Amadeus travel-services breach was maliciously exploited, after Japan Airlines reported exposure of about 92,000 customer records. Reports also identify impact at All Nippon Airways, Asiana Airlines and Korean Air. The breach occurred between August 2023 and September 2026.
items.impact: JAL flights, ticketing and check-in were not disrupted, and payment-card numbers were not exposed. Travel details and, for about 2,000 JAL customers, passport and contact information were accessed. The wider airline impact is still unclear.
items.what_next: Amadeus and affected airlines are determining how many customers and organizations were involved. Customers may receive additional notices and should be cautious of messages using real travel details.

finance.intro: A possible large cryptocurrency theft is under investigation, while a separate platform restored trading after confirmed customer losses. Belgium’s tax portal also remains disrupted during an investigation.

items.headline: Binance investigates a possible cryptocurrency theft of billions
items.what_happened: Binance is investigating transfers from several of its digital-asset wallets. Researchers estimate that as much as $5.8 billion is linked to the suspected attacker, but the exchange has not confirmed that the transfers were unauthorized or that customer funds were lost.
items.impact: Binance says customer funds are safe. The amount involved and effect on customers remain unclear. Stablecoin issuers froze more than $2.3 billion connected to the incident.
items.what_next: The exchange, law enforcement and blockchain analysts are determining whether this was a breach and the actual amount involved.

items.headline: Polymarket resumes trading after cryptocurrency-draining code attack
items.what_happened: Harmful code from a compromised monitoring provider targeted logged-in Polymarket users. The platform paused trading for about an hour, fixed the issue and said it would reimburse affected traders.
items.impact: About $2.5 million in assets was traced to a suspected attacker wallet. The number of affected users and final loss are not known. Trading has resumed.
items.what_next: Polymarket is investigating the supplier breach and will clarify how reimbursement will work.

items.headline: Belgium extends tax filing deadline after taking portal offline
items.what_happened: Belgium suspended its MyMinfin tax portal after an October 28 cyberattack. The ministry is investigating and said taxpayers affected by the October 31 deadline will receive more time.
items.impact: Online tax filing and related services may be unavailable. Officials have found no indication of stolen data so far.
items.what_next: Authorities will announce a new deadline and report whether the investigation finds any information exposure.

internet.intro: A Japanese internet provider confirmed a large customer-record breach, while a short-lived trading incident and a Belgian government portal outage affected online services.

items.headline: Sony’s Japanese internet provider confirms 2.6 million records were stolen
items.what_happened: Attackers entered the So-net member database on October 19 and took records belonging to about 2.6 million current and former customers. The exposed information includes names, birth dates, contact details and internet connection IDs. Passwords for about 54,000 separate email accounts were also exposed.
items.impact: Those email users had to change passwords because attackers could otherwise access their mail. No internet outage was reported. Credit-card data and bank PINs were not stored, although 16 records included bank-account details.
items.what_next: Sony is investigating the entry point and has reported the incident to Japan’s privacy regulator. Further customer notices may follow.

items.headline: Belgium’s main online tax service remains offline after an attack
items.what_happened: The finance ministry took MyMinfin offline on October 28 while investigating a cyberattack. The service handles tax and other financial administration.
items.impact: People may be unable to complete tax tasks online. The ministry extended the filing deadline and said there is no current indication that data was stolen.
items.what_next: Investigators are checking the scope of the incident and will announce a revised deadline and restoration information.

items.headline: Japan Airlines booking breach is linked to several other carriers
items.what_happened: The Amadeus travel-services breach that exposed Japan Airlines customer data was confirmed as an actual malicious intrusion. New reporting also identifies All Nippon Airways, Asiana Airlines and Korean Air as affected by the same supplier flaw.
items.impact: JAL reported no flight, ticketing or check-in outage and no exposed card numbers. Travel details and some passport and contact information were accessed. The total number of affected travelers across airlines is unknown.
items.what_next: Amadeus and the airlines are investigating the wider scope and may issue more customer notices.

items.headline: Binance confirms major cryptocurrency theft and pauses withdrawals
items.what_happened: Binance says attackers used access linked to a compromised employee laptop to submit unauthorized withdrawals. items.headline: Malicious Claude coding extension reached up to 5,000 developers
items.what_happened: A modified version of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension was distributed through Cursor’s marketplace for about 11 hours on October 29. items.impact: Up to 5,000 developers may have installed the package. The malware could expose development computers and information used by their projects. No wider distribution through Microsoft’s or Open VSX’s marketplaces was confirmed.
items.what_next: Cursor is contacting affected users and reviewing other marketplace extensions. The investigation may establish how the package was published and whether any developer credentials or project data were accessed.

items.headline: Florida financial-aid breach exposes Social Security numbers of 4.9 million people

items.impact: Nearly 5 million people who applied for Florida financial aid may face identity-theft and fraud risks. Student aid, scholarships, loans, tuition payments and aid disbursements were not disrupted.
items.what_next: Florida officials are investigating with state law-enforcement and technology agencies. More details and notifications may follow. The department says affected people should watch their credit reports and financial accounts.

items.headline: Trezor warns that a reseller may have sold an altered crypto wallet

items.impact: A tampered device could expose a wallet’s recovery phrase and allow cryptocurrency theft. Trezor says it knows of no stolen funds linked to this case. The warning applies to devices bought through CryptoBilis from March 2026 onward.
items.what_next: Trezor is waiting to examine the device and is investigating the reseller relationship. Buyers may receive replacement or voucher offers. The company may issue further warnings if the suspected alteration is confirmed.

items.what_happened: Google and partners say Videostrong deliberately built a hidden control mechanism into Android TV boxes over several years. The devices were used for advertising fraud, secret internet routing and additional malware. Disrupting the operators also cut access to at least 10 million other compromised devices.
items.impact: Owners may have had internet traffic routed through their home connections without consent, while devices could download malware or expose personal information. Google did not report household outages or identify all affected models.
items.what_next: Google and partners will continue investigating the manufacturer and related malware networks. Further notices may clarify which brands and models were involved and what owners should expect.

items.headline: Hacked supermarket freezers spoiled food across six European countries
items.what_happened: Attackers remotely changed refrigeration settings at more than 115 supermarkets and smaller food shops in Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia. Some freezers shut down, switched to defrosting or produced heat. The incident occurred overnight into Monday, November 2.
items.impact: Stores discarded spoiled frozen food and managers had to intervene early. Most affected stores stayed open, but some stock was lost. No nationwide food shortage was reported.
items.what_next: Retailers and refrigeration technicians are restoring affected equipment and investigating whether the incidents share one cause. More stores or product losses may be identified.

items.what_happened: On Sunday, compromised emergency-alert apps in Ukraine and Russia sent false warnings about radiation, chemical threats, fighting and nuclear attacks. Ukraine temporarily disabled alerts, while Russia said its main warning system was unaffected.
items.impact: Millions of app users could have been frightened or misled. Ukraine gradually restored basic alerts, but its map remained partly disabled. Sirens, text messages, television and radio warnings continued normally in the affected countries.
items.what_next: App developers and authorities are investigating and adding protections. Service availability and the reliability of supplementary app alerts may change as recovery continues.

items.impact: The state says medical records, Social Security numbers and financial information were not involved. Data theft could not be ruled out, creating possible identity-fraud or targeted-scam risks for affected Medicaid recipients.

items.headline: Russian cloud provider rebuilds after destructive attack cuts services
items.what_happened: Beget said attackers reached its management systems on November 1 and erased data across its cloud infrastructure. The company disconnected servers and is rebuilding from scratch. More than 200,000 customers use its hosting, cloud and domain services.
items.impact: About 60% of shared hosting and 40% of dedicated servers had been restored, but recovery remains incomplete. Some virtual-server data may be permanently lost, and online shops, media sites and schools may remain unavailable or impaired.
items.what_next: Beget is checking roughly 1,000 servers before bringing them back. Further updates may show which customer data can be recovered and when remaining services return.

items.headline: France blames Iran for supermarket attacks that spoiled food and sparked fires
items.what_happened: France attributed October 11–12 attacks on refrigeration controls at about 700 stores and food businesses to an Iranian Revolutionary Guard cyber unit. Authorities say the attacks caused extensive food losses and at least 15 fires. The later November attacks remain unattributed.
items.impact: French authorities estimate tens of millions of euros in food losses. Large chains, butchers, a slaughterhouse and food-processing sites were affected. Small hydroelectric sites were also targeted, with moderate disruption reported.
items.what_next: France plans diplomatic action and possible European sanctions. A judicial investigation is opening, while authorities may identify more damage. The November wave is still under investigation.

items.headline: Qubole cloud access was used to enter customer accounts and copy data
items.what_happened: An attacker used trusted access belonging to Qubole, a cloud data platform, to enter several customers’ Amazon cloud accounts between October 14 and 26. The attacker searched stored secrets and copied information from cloud storage.
items.impact: Organizations connected to Qubole may have had passwords, access keys and stored business data exposed. The reports do not identify affected customers or show disruption to public services. The scale of the data loss is unclear.
items.what_next: Qubole and its owner had not publicly explained the incident when reported. Further investigation may identify affected customers, the entry point and whether the activity has stopped.

items.headline: Malicious Swarm software releases exposed users to wallet theft
items.what_happened: Attackers used Ethersphere’s release process to publish two harmful versions of Swarm tools on November 9. The releases could steal wallet keys and install control software on Windows, Mac and Linux computers. Both releases were withdrawn within hours.
items.impact: The number of infected computers is unknown. No stolen funds were reported, but a computer that ran the affected software may have exposed wallet keys and other information. The malicious desktop release reached at least 65 downloads, including researchers.
items.what_next: The project released a clean replacement and is investigating the stolen release credentials. Users and organizations may receive more information about exposed keys, downloads and any confirmed theft.

items.headline: Revolve says payment-card breach affected 1.5 million people
items.what_happened: Revolve revised its estimate for the September 11 online-store intrusion to 1,515,073 people, up sharply from earlier state filings. Names, addresses and stored card numbers and expiration dates may have been copied.
items.impact: Customers who saved payment cards may face unauthorized charges or targeted scams. Revolve has not reported fraudulent transactions, and shopping service was not interrupted.
items.what_next: The company is notifying affected people and working with investigators. Further filings may refine the count or confirm whether stolen card details were misused.

overview.intro: Fresh reporting expands the known impact of a certificate-authority incident, confirms limited exposure of Notion AI conversations, and reports a breach at a Maersk legacy system. No broad power, water or household communications outage is confirmed.

items.headline: More website and code-signing certificates revoked after eMudhra review
items.what_happened: eMudhra revoked eight more certificate-authority certificates on November 7 after finding that a key-transfer script handled their private keys outside required protections. Six supported website certificates and two supported code signing. The earlier eight certificates had already been weakened.
items.impact: The affected customer certificates have been replaced or moved to another provider. Browsers and operating systems already block the first compromised group. eMudhra says it has found no evidence of malicious use, so no forged websites or signed malware are confirmed.
items.what_next: An independent review is due by December 4. eMudhra plans to stop issuing certificates under its remaining hierarchy by November 16, while its full key inventory is due November 30.

items.what_happened: Notion found that Fireworks AI, its outside AI infrastructure provider, exposed chat transcripts from the Insights feature during an October breach. The chats were mostly unattributed, meaning they were not linked to a person or workspace in the exposed data.
items.impact: Less than 1% of Notion users are reported to be affected. The disclosure adds private workplace conversation content to the customer and project information already known to have been reached at Fireworks. Notion says its cloud service remains available.
items.what_next: Notion has disabled the Insights dataset and notified affected workspace owners. Its investigation and customer review may clarify which conversations were included.

items.what_next: The investigation is continuing. Maersk may notify customers if it confirms affected records or a wider impact. Unexpected messages about the incident could be scams.

items.headline: Microsoft 365 outage disrupts email and workplace services worldwide

items.impact: At least 288 devices in 48 organizations were affected, including systems managed by service providers. The campaign could give attackers continuing access to business computers and networks. The exact number of wider victims is still unclear.

items.headline: Attackers stole cloud credentials through thousands of GitHub projects
items.what_happened: Attackers used stolen access to 4,837 GitHub accounts to test more than 61,000 repositories. In at least 1,806 repositories, they inserted code into automated build jobs that collected cloud, developer and artificial-intelligence service credentials.
items.impact: Organizations whose automated jobs ran the code may have lost access keys and private project information. Some affected accounts belonged to major companies and public institutions. The campaign also caused malicious changes to be published in some software packages.
items.what_next: Researchers are still determining the full reach of the campaign. Further notices may identify additional affected repositories, software releases and organizations whose credentials were taken.

items.headline: U.S. authorities seize $1.2 billion linked to Binance cryptocurrency theft
items.what_happened: The U.S. Justice Department obtained court approval to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance last month. Several cryptocurrency platforms have frozen about $2.7 billion in total.
items.impact: The action may prevent a substantial part of the stolen funds from being laundered or moved. It does not restore all losses, and the theft itself remains under investigation. Binance customers’ normal service impact was not reported.
items.what_next: Authorities and cryptocurrency companies are continuing to trace, freeze and seize the remaining funds. The investigation may clarify how much money can ultimately be recovered.

items.headline: Attackers are probing N-able servers after new flaws were disclosed
items.what_happened: Researchers observed attempts to exploit newly disclosed flaws in N-able’s N-central remote-management software, including systems that had received the previous emergency update. The reported activity involved probing and attempted attacks; confirmed compromise of customer systems remains unclear.
items.impact: Organizations using exposed N-central servers could lose control of systems used to manage customer devices. N-able’s hosted environments had already been taken offline earlier in the week, so some service providers may still have reduced remote-management capability.
items.what_next: N-able is adding protective restrictions and investigating the reports. Further updates may confirm whether the observed attacks succeeded and when normal service can safely return.

items.what_happened: Minnesota Epilepsy Group says an August 10 incident exposed personal and health information belonging to about 82,574 people. Data may include names, birth dates, Social Security numbers, treatment details and insurance information.

items.what_next: Microsoft is monitoring the restarted servers and shifting traffic to alternate systems while investigating the cause.

items.what_happened: Investigators say attackers reached at least 288 devices in 48 organizations through ScreenConnect environments used by IT service providers. The attackers installed unauthorized remote-access software and designed malware to spread through technician support sessions.
items.impact: Affected businesses could lose control of work computers and networks. The campaign may also reach other customers managed by the same provider. No household phone or internet outage is reported.

items.what_happened: Apify, a web-scraping and browser-automation service, found unauthorized access to parts of its internal systems between November 9 and 10. It rotated some customer access tokens and proxy passwords and asked some users to reset extra login checks.
items.impact: Affected customers may temporarily lose access to connected services or need to reconnect integrations. Apify says it has found no sign that stored account data was affected, but the full scope remains under review.
items.what_next: Apify is investigating and will contact affected customers when integrations can safely be reconnected. Further notices may clarify whether customer information was accessed.

items.headline: Belarusian cloud attack disrupted business websites and email for days
items.what_happened: ActiveCloud said ransomware encrypted parts of its infrastructure earlier this week. The attack disrupted cloud hosting, virtual servers, corporate email and customer support for businesses in Belarus. The company says its main services were restored Friday, but some customers are still recovering their systems.
items.impact: Businesses using ActiveCloud may still have trouble reaching websites, email or virtual machines. A news site and the Belarusian Domino’s website were among services reported as affected. ActiveCloud says it has found no evidence that customer data was stolen.
items.what_next: ActiveCloud is continuing recovery for individual customers and investigating how the attackers entered. Service availability may improve, but some virtual servers may take longer to restore.

items.headline: Destructive attacks wiped data after Check Point gateways were breached
items.what_happened: Attacks began October 30 against Israeli organizations and expanded internationally on November 2. Attackers entered some Check Point gateways through flaws in widely used website software, gained deeper control, and in some cases moved to VMware servers to delete data. The second wave was not reported to include wiping.
items.impact: Organizations hit in the destructive wave could lose files and disrupt services running on affected servers. Check Point said the attacks reached a couple dozen customers, but the number with deleted data is unclear. No specific public-service outage is confirmed.
items.what_next: Investigators are assessing the victims and the attackers’ broader actions. Attribution remains uncertain, and later findings may clarify whether the destructive activity was the main goal or a diversion.

items.headline: Police seize criminal servers and millions of stolen logins
items.what_happened: An international operation seized 235 servers and 257 domains linked to Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC. These criminal tools infected computers, stole passwords and helped ransomware gangs reach victims. Authorities identified about 6.4 million stolen login details linked to more than 40,000 victims.
items.impact: The takedown disrupts services used to infect computers and sell stolen access. It does not guarantee that criminals no longer possess the stolen logins or that infected devices are clean. Gootloader was linked to at least 44 U.S. ransomware victims and about $28.8 million in losses.
items.what_next: Authorities and internet providers are notifying possible victims and sharing stolen-login data with checking services. Further notifications and investigations may identify additional infected computers or misuse of the stolen credentials.

items.headline: Healthcare software breach exposed records for 58,000 patients
items.what_happened: Dorsata, a healthcare technology company, newly reported that attackers exploited a previously unknown flaw in its Metabase reporting software between August 10 and 12. The attackers reached a database containing patient information belonging to healthcare-provider customers.
items.impact: About 58,249 people are affected. Exposed records may include names, addresses, birth dates, medical histories, treatment details, medicines, vaccinations and insurance information. No misuse of the information has been found, and the incident date is earlier than this report.
items.what_next: Dorsata and its partners are notifying affected people and continuing the investigation. Further notices may clarify which patients and healthcare providers were involved.

items.headline: Apify says attackers accessed some customer accounts and stored data
items.what_happened: Apify, a web-automation company, said attackers entered its internal systems on November 9 and 10 using a compromised credential. The company confirmed that some customer personal information or stored data was accessed, though it has not given a victim count.
items.impact: Affected customers may have had names, email addresses, billing details, account activity, phone numbers, password hashes, extra-login recovery codes and sign-in tokens exposed. Full payment-card numbers and security codes were not exposed, according to the reported notification. Service disruption was not reported.
items.what_next: Apify is contacting affected customers and continuing its investigation. The scope may grow as the company identifies which accounts and stored data were reached.

items.headline: U.S. flights halted nationwide after air-traffic communications failure
items.what_happened: The Federal Aviation Administration halted departing flights at U.S. airports Friday after a communications problem affected all air-route traffic-control centers. The cause is unclear, and officials have not said it was a cyberattack. International arrivals were being handled case by case.
items.impact: Travelers may face delays, cancellations and difficulty getting reliable flight updates. The disruption affects air travel, not household communications. Its duration and total number of affected flights are unclear.
items.what_next: FAA technicians are investigating and are expected to provide updates. Flight operations may change as communications are restored.

items.headline: Osaka warns that more than one million city email addresses were exposed
items.what_happened: Hackers accessed Arara, an email-distribution service used by contractor TKC for Osaka’s online administrative platform. Email addresses of people who received city messages between July and October 31 were exposed. The wider Arara attack affected many customers and reportedly exposed 77 million addresses.
items.impact: Affected residents may receive convincing fake messages pretending to come from Osaka, banks or card companies. No loss of city services was reported, but the city says all 2.8 million residents should be cautious about suspicious messages.
items.what_next: Osaka and the service providers are investigating. More affected organizations and misuse of the exposed addresses may be identified.

items.headline: Three cryptocurrency wallets sold by one reseller had hidden data-stealing parts
items.what_happened: Trezor confirmed that three Safe 5 wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained hidden circuit boards. The parts could copy wallet recovery phrases shown on the screen and send them over mobile networks. The devices were bought between August 20 and September 23.
items.impact: No owner has reported lost funds, but a stolen recovery phrase could let criminals take cryptocurrency. Trezor says the confirmed implants were limited to this reseller and model so far.
items.what_next: Trezor is examining other reported devices and offering replacements to people who bought from CryptoBilis since March. Its investigation may reveal more affected wallets or any stolen funds.

items.headline: Drone maker’s update system was breached, disrupting German military operations
items.what_happened: German defense company Quantum Systems confirmed a cyberattack in late October. Reports say attackers used a malicious update through the company’s QBase mission-planning software. German military drones were reportedly grounded as a precaution, though the number that installed the update is unclear.
items.impact: Drone operations were temporarily disrupted while the company and authorities checked the software. The reporting does not confirm that attackers controlled deployed drones or caused physical harm.
items.what_next: German authorities and the company are investigating the update server and its customers. They may clarify how many systems received the update and when operations fully resume.

items.headline: Texas university confirms hackers stole personal information
items.what_happened: The University of Texas at Arlington said hackers breached its systems last month and stole personal information. The university has not yet said what data was taken or how many people were affected. An online form service used for registrations, requests and surveys remains offline.
items.impact: Students and employees may face delays using that service. The university serves more than 41,000 students, but it has not confirmed how many people are in the stolen data or reported disruption to classes or core services.
items.what_next: The university is identifying affected people and reviewing the impact on other systems. It says it will contact people directly when the review is complete.

items.what_next: The city and its providers are investigating the wider breach and may identify more affected customers or misuse of the addresses.

items.headline: Malicious coding extension reached up to 5,000 Cursor users
items.what_happened: Cursor said attackers used a stolen key from its AI provider, Fireworks, to access internal data and publish altered copies of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension on October 29. items.what_next: Cursor says it removed the extensions, rebuilt its marketplace and moved AI processing away from Fireworks. Its investigation and customer notices may clarify which users installed the altered versions and whether the hidden access worked.

Exposed information includes names, driver’s license numbers, birth dates and addresses. The incident occurred in October and was linked in reporting to the Fireworks provider breach already covered.
items.impact: Affected drivers face a higher risk of identity theft and targeted scams. The report does not describe a ride-service outage or stolen passenger data.
items.what_next: Uber has cut the affected data connection and is investigating. Additional notices may clarify support for affected drivers and whether other records were accessed.

items.headline: Remote-support attacks could spread from technicians to customers
items.what_happened: Attackers have targeted ScreenConnect systems used by managed service providers since at least October 20. Huntress saw 688,000 attempts against 42 provider servers, while a separate wave affected 205 computers across 41 organizations. The attacks can place harmful files on a technician’s computer during a remote session.
items.impact: If a provider’s technician computer is compromised, attackers could potentially reach multiple customer networks. The reports do not confirm a broad customer outage or how many customer systems were successfully taken over.
items.what_next: ConnectWise says attacks continue against some older installations and is investigating affected environments. Further reporting may identify additional providers or customer networks involved.

items.headline: Dental provider reports personal and medical data breach affecting 341,049
items.what_happened: Access Dental Management, which provides care in Texas and several other states, newly reported that attackers accessed its network from May 1 to May 4. The exposed information may include names, addresses, birth dates, Social Security numbers, medical details and insurance information.
items.impact: People included in the confirmed count could face identity theft, fraud or targeted medical scams. The provider reported 341,049 affected people, while a larger possible total has not been confirmed. No care disruption was reported.
items.what_next: Access Dental Management is sending notices and reviewing the incident. More information may clarify whether the affected total exceeds the currently reported count.

overview.intro: Fresh reports describe a Japanese research supercomputer outage after a breach, a continuing attack on the Tor privacy network, and active exploitation of N-central systems. Google also reports that attackers are using artificial intelligence to speed up real intrusions. No broad household power, water or communications outage is confirmed.

items.headline: Japan takes Fugaku supercomputer offline after a data breach
items.what_happened: The breach occurred between November 10 and 13. RIKEN says an intruder reached several Fugaku servers and planted malware targeting user data. Names and login details for 4,222 Fugaku users and 375 Rikyu users were exposed, along with some stored access keys and research files.
items.impact: Fugaku has been offline since November 14, so researchers cannot use it for work such as drug discovery, weather forecasting and scientific simulations. RIKEN found no confirmed theft of research results or further unauthorized access.
items.what_next: RIKEN is investigating how the intruder entered and will restore service only after safety checks. Affected users may receive further information about exposed data and access keys.

items.headline: Ongoing attack slows the Tor privacy network
items.what_happened: The Tor Project says a large flood of connection requests has overwhelmed most network relays. It released an emergency update to improve defenses, but did not identify the attacker or say when the attack began.
items.impact: People using Tor may experience slower connections or difficulty reaching websites. The report does not describe a general internet outage or evidence that users’ identities were exposed.
items.what_next: Tor says it is working on more defenses and expects additional updates. The network’s availability and performance may continue to change while the attack continues.

items.headline: Attackers exploit N-central flaws to install cryptocurrency miners
items.what_happened: Attackers began using earlier N-central flaws after technical details were published, placing cryptocurrency-mining software on vulnerable servers. N-able has now blocked the older access route and issued a broader security update for its remote-management platform.
items.impact: Organizations using affected N-central systems could face unauthorized computing use, slower systems or follow-on compromise. The supplied reports do not identify affected organizations or any household service outage.
items.what_next: N-able says hosted systems were updated and is investigating the active attacks. Further reports may clarify how many customer environments were reached and whether other harmful activity occurred.

items.headline: Google reports faster, more automated attacks against real organizations
items.what_happened: Google says criminal and government-backed groups are using artificial-intelligence tools to scan targets, find weaknesses and carry out parts of intrusions automatically. It observed these tools in attacks involving aerospace companies and organizations in Asia, while Chinese groups are developing similar systems.
items.impact: The tools may shorten the time between a software flaw becoming public and attackers using it. No specific household outage, stolen-customer count or confirmed harm to the public is reported in this update.
items.what_next: Google expects attackers to automate more stages of intrusions. Investigations may identify additional affected organizations and clarify how much activity was successful rather than attempted.

overview.intro: Fresh reporting confirms a major credit-union data exposure, a compromised Microsoft developer package, and active attacks against business software. A Russian espionage campaign also shows how stolen cloud data was used to target a second organization. No broad power, water or household communications outage is confirmed.

items.headline: Credit-union supplier breach exposed members’ payee information
items.what_happened: Wellington IT, a supplier to about 50 credit unions, was attacked between October 2 and 4. Officials say data from about 40 Irish credit unions was exposed. The attacker accessed saved payee records using valid credentials. The supplier reportedly lacked logs showing exactly whose data was taken.
items.impact: The number of affected people is unknown. Exposed records may include payee names, bank account numbers, international account numbers, addresses and payment references. Passwords, payment cards, account credentials and funds were not affected according to the reported notices. Members face phishing, impersonation and fraud risks.
items.what_next: Credit unions and investigators may clarify the affected records and number of people. Further notices could explain support for members and whether individual accounts need additional protection.

items.headline: Malicious Microsoft package may have stolen developers’ cloud credentials
items.what_happened: Attackers uploaded two harmful versions of Microsoft’s Agent Framework package to the Python Package Index on November 17. The package ran credential-stealing code whenever Python started, even if the framework was not used. The releases were later quarantined.
items.impact: Developers who installed either version may have exposed cloud, source-code and service credentials. The package has about 190,000 to 200,000 monthly downloads, but the number of affected users and confirmed thefts is unclear. This was a compromise of a trusted software distribution channel, not a reported consumer outage.
items.what_next: Microsoft and package researchers are investigating how publishing access was obtained and whether credentials were used. Further findings may identify affected development environments or downstream services.

items.headline: Attackers are exploiting a flaw in Apache Roller blogging servers
items.what_happened: The Apache Software Foundation says attackers are actively exploiting a flaw in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4. The flaw can let an unauthenticated attacker take control of a vulnerable server. Apache has not said who is behind the attacks or how many servers were compromised.
items.impact: Organizations running affected Roller servers could face website changes, data theft or wider network compromise. No specific affected organizations, public outage or confirmed stolen data was reported.
items.what_next: Apache and affected organizations may disclose more about the attacks and compromised servers. The scale of the campaign remains unclear.

items.headline: Attackers are using a Puppet management flaw to reach managed systems
items.what_happened: A critical flaw in Perforce Puppet has been exploited against enterprise management servers. Puppet can control software and settings across many devices, so a compromised server may be used to alter systems it manages. The flaw was fixed on November 3 and was added to the U.S. exploited-vulnerability list on November 17.
items.impact: Organizations using vulnerable, misconfigured Puppet systems could face mass unauthorized software changes, data theft or ransomware. The reports do not identify victims or confirm disruption to public services or household products.
items.what_next: Perforce and investigators may clarify how widely the flaw was exploited and whether attackers changed managed systems. The related OpenVox platform was also affected, according to the reports.

items.headline: Stolen cloud data helped Russian hackers target a second organization
items.what_happened: Google reported that the Russia-linked Cold Relic group used employee lists, messages and other information stolen from a U.S. organization in late 2025. The group impersonated an employee when approaching a second U.S. organization and then stole data from that organization’s cloud storage.
items.impact: The organizations were not named, and the stolen information was not described. The incident shows that a breach at one organization can make convincing scams against its employees, partners and contacts more likely. No public service outage was reported.
items.what_next: Google and affected organizations may identify the victims and explain what data was accessed. Further investigations could reveal additional organizations targeted through the stolen relationships.

overview.intro: A cryptocurrency scam used a fake livestream and an AI-generated celebrity video to persuade people to send money. Coinbase says it stopped most attempted transfers, but some funds may still have reached the scammers. No broad power, water or communications outage is confirmed.

items.headline: Fake Elon Musk livestream prompts millions in attempted crypto transfers
items.what_happened: During a fake Tesla livestream, scammers used an AI-generated video of Elon Musk and promised to double any cryptocurrency sent to a displayed wallet. Coinbase says hundreds of customers tried to transfer millions of dollars over about two hours.
items.impact: Coinbase blocked about $4.7 million, or 91% of attempted transfers. The amount that reached scammers and the number of affected customers are unclear. Cryptocurrency transfers are usually difficult to reverse.
items.what_next: Coinbase may clarify how much cryptocurrency was successfully received by the scammers. The incident could lead to more warnings about deepfake videos, fake livestreams and QR-code giveaway scams.

finance.intro: A cryptocurrency exchange says it blocked most transfers linked to a fake celebrity giveaway, though the final loss remains unclear.

items.headline: Coinbase blocks most transfers in fake celebrity crypto giveaway
items.what_happened: Scammers used an AI-generated Elon Musk video in a fake Tesla livestream to promise viewers double their cryptocurrency. Hundreds of Coinbase customers attempted transfers during the roughly two-hour scam.
items.impact: Coinbase says it stopped $4.7 million in attempted transfers. Some cryptocurrency may have reached the scammers, but the total is not known. No customer account takeover was reported; people sent the money themselves after being deceived.
items.what_next: Coinbase may report the amount that was not blocked. The exchange and other services may continue investigating similar deepfake promotions tied to live events.
